releases.name: v1.5.1-native-vl.7 — safe chat-prefix checkpoints
releases.body:
Safe common-prefix reuse for divergent Chat Completions, addressing [issue #12](https://github.com/Approaching-AI/AIMA-AMD395-Qwen36-35B-Linux-Engine/issues/12).

The `你好` → `你好，你是谁` reproduction now restores 15 prompt tokens and computes only the remaining 11. Checkpoints preserve KV, recurrent, convolution and hidden state together, retain media-identity isolation, and expose actual restore bytes/time.

Validation on the exact engine with the frozen portable userspace:

- Both four-owner and one-owner profiles pass: 52 generation pairs and 68 full-vocabulary logits comparisons, independently reproduced from public raw files. Maximum KLD 0.0035071; every top-1 matches.
- The long shared-system corpus shows approximately 3.37x median partial-hit TTFT speedup without observed decode regression. Peak GTT remains below 96 GiB.
- All 19 text-matrix cells pass, including the maximum total-token window. Minimum prefill/decode retention is 1.03246 / 1.03405 against the published matrix baseline.
- 11 chat-protocol checks, 12 HTTP checks, isolated archive execution, a full one-hour/360-request mixed-workload soak, exact v1.5.1 rollback, and repository/security/evidence gates pass. The soak loads the model once, shows zero post-warm RSS growth and shuts down cleanly.

The runtime archive is `aima-engine-native-portable-5a699d1600cc.tar.zst` (345,552,799 bytes). SHA-256:

```text
fb88242d52b6d3a1c152c8c7119c641275090fb7210e672d6c3fae358d215303
```

Download the matching checksum sidecar. The separate `aima-engine-v1.5.1-native-vl.7-public-evidence.tar.zst` and its sidecar contain the sealed public qualification records and raw data. Model weights are not included.

The immutable package tag points to `9bd8a0fabcf2fc6ef1b882c10b04390c0e31fb00`; native source is `edb584ee16f0ee1fc5f902459598b9446d96387e`. The additive evidence commit preserves both identities.

Scope: up to three saved eligible checkpoints per LRU owner, with 32-token alignment for longer prefixes and conservative cold fallback for unsafe short cross-block continuations. This is not arbitrary-token radix caching or universal BF16 bitwise equivalence; use `--disable-prefix-cache` for the cold partition. Historical `.4` cold/VL and two-host evidence remains explicitly inherited only for unchanged arithmetic, kernels and userspace. See [release provenance and limits](https://github.com/skyguan92/AIMA-AMD395-Qwen36-35B-Linux-Engine/blob/main/docs/RELEASE.md).

releases.name: v1.5.1-native-vl.4 — portable native vision-language serving
releases.body:
## What changed

This is the first portable native AMD395 release for the fixed Qwen3.6-35B-A3B model with complete image, video, and mixed-media serving in the same resident native process as text generation.

- native media admission and decoding, the 27-block vision stack, merger, M-RoPE injection, language prefill/decode, SSE, and function tools;
- seeded positive-temperature, top-p, full-vocabulary BF16 sampling in addition to the certified greedy path;
- batch size 1 and the 262,144-token total context window;

releases.body:
## What changed

The release also preserves the v1.5.0 resident prefix LRU, live SSE streaming,

releases.name: v1.5.0 — resident short-context serving
releases.body:
## What changed

- A q8192 resident service now keeps q1024/q2048/q4096/q8192 AOT prefill buckets loaded and selects the largest fitting bucket per request.
- Exact request-prefix reuse is now a capacity-bounded LRU: four entries at q8192, two at medium long contexts and one at the largest windows.
- Health, CLI and request metrics expose resident buckets, cache capacity and executed AOT-prefill tokens.
- Release qualification now includes a privacy-safe, frozen MMLU-256 scorecard paired against identical GB10 vLLM prompt-token hashes.

## Qualified result

- All 19 batch-1 performance cells passed; minimum frozen-baseline retention was `1.013x` prefill and `0.9858x` decode.
- Nine-context full-vocabulary correctness passed with top-1 agreement everywhere and worst KLD `0.002174 < 0.005`.
- The exact q8192 128-token completion matched.
- MMLU-256 scored `216/256` (`84.375%`), equal to the frozen GB10 vLLM reference, with zero invalid answers and all 256 prompt-token hashes matched.
- SSE streaming, OpenAI function tools, disconnect recovery, variable prompts, multi-entry LRU, startup and isolated bundle checks passed.
- The checksum-identical archive reproduced on a second AMD395: q8192 cold prefill `1722 tok/s`, decode512 `32.36 tok/s`, exact completion and resident HTTP all passed.

## Runtime boundary

The archive is self-contained at userspace level: no host Python, PyTorch, vLLM, Triton, Transformers or ROCm userspace is required. The host still needs Linux x86-64, AMDGPU/KFD/render access, Radeon 8060S (`gfx1151`), the documented 96 GiB GTT setup and the separately obtained pinned model checkpoint. Model weights are not included.

```bash
sha256sum -c aima-engine-native-portable-86e806e8bc5d.tar.zst.sha256
tar --zstd -xf aima-engine-native-portable-86e806e8bc5d.tar.zst
cd aima-engine-native-portable-86e806e8bc5d
./bin/aima-engine doctor --model-dir /srv/models/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B --json
./bin/aima-engine serve --model-dir /srv/models/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B --context-tokens 8192
```

decision: Leave K16-major preparation disabled. Both complete product runs pass all512 original GB10 tokens, actual callbacks and exact first144/logit10.375, but enabling the layout adds1082.6284ms to callback TTFT and989.57ms to completed dense correction in this pair. Candidate counts and allocated view sizes match. Do not polish this slower layout; investigate whether native completion waits contribute materially across providers before another arithmetic replacement.
limitations: A single paired observation is not a repeatability or sustained-throughput claim. No retained performance target is recovered.
Preparation and cleanup remain inside actual callback TTFT; dense correction markers include preparation and completion observation but not their allocation/cleanup.
No new long-context, saved-checkpoint, package, HTTP or one-hour soak acceptance follows. The optional layout defaults off.
The earlier absolute-product admission counterexample remains a separate disabled route. No change to its multiplier or to the correctness authority is made.
